subject: Post-demo: runtime snapshots, latency p99s & prompt-regression plan
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@mediqai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@mediqai.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick ask

Thanks for the demo today — really helpful to see the end-to-end latency. A couple quick asks as we ingest the deck: are you able to share the raw perf snapshots you ran against our sample traffic (seq lengths ~64 / tokenization similar to our pipeline)? Also want to understand any known quality regressions when we use the prompt templates we shared (especially the triage prompt that compresses notes).

Can you drop the perf CSV and the exact model configs you tested? If there's a short note on guidance (batching / prefix cache settings) that would be great.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Director of ML, MediQ AI
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@mediqai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-06T18:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick ask

Ellen — appreciate the clear asks. Attaching the CSV export and the prompt-set bundle (links below + files attached). High-level summary up front: we tested three candidate model variants against your sample traces (seq ~64, mixed batch sizes, nctx 4k):

- redwood-7b-q4f16 (int4 optimized): TPS ~ 420 (seq64), p50/p90/p99: 9ms / 36ms / 98ms. Best cost/TPS for smaller payoffs, quality equivalent on short triage prompts in our A/B eval.
- redwood-13b-8bit (aml).TPU-tuned: TPS ~ 210, p50/p90/p99: 14ms / 52ms / 140ms. Slightly higher quality on long-context summarization prompts.
- redwood-65b-8bit: TPS ~ 45, p50/p90/p99: 48ms / 180ms / 420ms. Highest quality but >3x cost vs 13b for your workload.

Notes on regression risk: the compression/abstractive triage prompt you shared compresses clinical notes aggressively. In our regression sweep vs your golden set: 7b-q4f16 had a small semantic drift on low-frequency entity recall (F1 delta -0.04) for extremely noisy inputs. 13b-8bit showed stable recall but occasional hallucinated timestamps on OCR-noisy fields. We include the eval slices (CSV) so you can inspect by case type.

Recommended pilot: start on redwood-13b-8bit as a balanced candidate (latency within your P99 SLO if we apply per-customer prefix cache + batch=8). If cost needs to be constrained, we can run 7b-q4f16 with a stricter post-filter and an entity-check step.

Attachments: mediq-benchmark-20261106.csv, prompt-sets_mediq_v1.zip, redwood-p10-perf-profiles.pdf
Links: https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/redwood-7b-q4f16 (profile), https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/mediq/prompt-sets-v1

Next steps I propose: 1) short pilot-config doc from us by EOD Monday 11/9, 2) run a 72-hour pilot on a 2-node dedicated pool (we'll scope cost), 3) set up a weekly regression check with your ML team and our Evals owner.

If you want, Marissa can spin up the pilot config and start the infra estimate.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@mediqai.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick ask

Ellen — dropping the pilot config and a concise checklist below. I've attached the pilot config YAML as well. High-level config we recommend for initial 72-hour run:

- model: redwood-13b-8bit
- nodes: 2 (dedicated)
- batch_policy: dynamic, target_batch=8, max_latency_ms=250
- prefix_cache: enabled, ttl=300s for repeated patient prefixes
- quant_mode: 8bit (we've validated kernel paths for this family)
- regen-policy: fall back to redwood-7b-q4f16 for cold-cache outages

Evals & regression guardrails (what we'll monitor):
- golden-set pass rate (per-case-type): target >= 96%
- entity recall per-slice (automated diff alerts if delta >= 2%)
- hallucination rate (free-text halluc detection): alert if >1.5% sustained over 1 hour

Action owners:
- Marissa: pilot config + infra estimate (EOD Mon 11/9)
- Ben: perf baseline and cost estimate (by Tue 11/10)
- Logan: prompt/guardrail recipes and smoke evals (by Mon 11/9)

Links to artifacts: perf CSV attached; perf profiles: https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/redwood-7b-q4f16 and https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/redwood-13b-8bit

If that plan looks good to you, we'll prepare the DocuSign SOW (short pilot SOW) and a one-page runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Ellen Park <ellen@mediqai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + quick ask

Perfect — thanks for the thorough breakdown. The pilot config looks sensible and aligns with our internal constraints. Please go ahead with the infra estimate and the SOW draft. We'll prioritize the golden set review on our side and loop Alex in for schedule.

One quick question: for the entity recall diffs, can you include per-case-type examples in the alert payload (so our triage team can immediately see examples)? That would speed triage.

Otherwise, we are good to proceed.

Ellen
